title: Within-place variance penalty: each member's pooled feature of one place, standardised against its spread across places, must be the same in all three surveys
hypothesis: The held-out 2024 photograph's usable-fix rate has sat at 7-12.5% through seven designs because the deployed feature of a place still changes with the survey, and no experiment has yet actually forbidden that. Experiment 3 tried (cosine between L2-normalised GAP features of the same position in different surveys) and was reverted, but a design-stage probe on the current champion's exported graph shows its metric could never have bitten: the RAW cosine between the pooled features of two DIFFERENT places is 0.70 (runs/_probe_exp9_wpv.py, 400 lattice positions, three TRAINING captures only, truedop_2024 never opened), because post-ReLU average-pooled features share a large positive common component. A same-place cross-survey cosine of 0.966 at epoch 1 and 0.935 at the end therefore meant 'the features are post-ReLU', not 'the three surveys agree' - and experiment 6 dismissed feature invariance on exactly that misreading ('the three training appearances were mapped to nearly the same vector'). Measured properly, with the batch mean removed, the champion's same-place cross-survey cosine is 0.69 and different-place is 0.00; as a within-place variance fraction of the per-dimension standardised feature (0 = identical feature in all surveys, 1 = a survey change moves the feature as far as a change of place), the three training surveys read 0.295, versus 0.152 for two independent draws of the photometric augmentation on one survey - the kept exposure/sharpness randomisation (exp 4) covers only half of what a change of survey does to the feature, and nothing in the training signal addresses the other half. The consequence is visible in the same probe: the SAME member, shown the SAME place at the SAME heading in two training surveys, names the same cell only 28-40% of the time (per-survey top1 34-46%), so even on photographs it trained on, the committee's agreement gate is largely gating survey-driven feature drift, not place knowledge; on a fourth survey the drift is at least as large and the cell beliefs land elsewhere. The remedy is the library's L2 rank-1 mechanism (cross-survey latent consistency, SSL4EO's top rung) implemented so that it cannot be satisfied for free: standardise every dimension of each member's 112-d pooled feature over the mini-batch (zero mean, unit variance), then penalise the variance that remains WITHIN a position across its three surveys' views, scaled so unrelated views read 1.0. Standardisation per dimension means a feature dimension that mostly encodes survey state (canopy greenness, shadow strength, colour pipeline) has within-place variance near its total variance and is penalised hardest, while a dimension that encodes place is nearly free - the trunk is pushed, over 218k paired views per epoch and all 2,970 places at once, to discard the directions along which the three surveys differ and keep the ones along which places differ. That is the domain-generalisation bet of this era stated as a loss: the fourth survey's deviations (season, sun angle, cars, pipeline) are assumed to lie largely in the span of the deviations between a summer standard DOP, a leaf-off true-ortho and an early-spring true-ortho, and a feature made invariant to that span transfers. No projector (a projector would let the deployed feature keep survey content and discard it only downstream, the opposite of what the linear cell head needs), no stop-gradient (the batch standard deviation in the denominator carries gradient on purpose: it is VICReg's variance term in disguise, and the 2,970-way cross-entropy on the same vector makes collapse impossible). It is one loss term on the existing committee; the exported graph is byte-identical.
method: Add INV_WEIGHT * invariance_loss(feat_k, n_caps) to each committee member's loss in model/train.py, where feat_k is that member's post-ReLU global-average-pooled 112-d trunk feature (the exact tensor its cell head reads) and invariance_loss standardises every dimension over the mini-batch, groups the rows by lattice position (all three training surveys of one position, same heading, independent photometric draws), and returns the within-position variance fraction scaled by K/(K-1). Mini-batches are rebuilt position-grouped (21 positions x 3 captures = 63 views, position-major rows) so every position in a batch is present in all three surveys - the same batching experiment 3 used, now on the device-side gpu_crops path. INV_WEIGHT = 10.0. Member.forward additionally returns the feature; CellLocNet.forward (the deployed decode) is unchanged and the ONNX must still read 3,942,411 bytes. Logged per epoch and per member: the mean within-place variance fraction (inv) and the cross-survey argmax agreement rate (fraction of positions on which the member names the same cell in all three surveys).
expected_outcome: Mechanical checks that must hold or the mechanism did not bite: the logged per-member within-place variance fraction (inv) falls from its epoch-1 value (predicted 0.35-0.50 on augmented views; the trained champion reads 0.295 on clean crops) to below 0.10 by epoch 8 for both members, and the logged cross-survey argmax agreement rises from ~0.3 (the champion's 0.28-0.40 on clean crops) to within 0.05 of each member's top1 - i.e. when a member knows a place it knows it in every survey. Exported bytes read exactly 3,942,411 and host latency ~2 ms. Primary (held-out truedop_2024): 1.096 -> predicted 0.95-1.06, for the first time in this era through usable_fix_rate: 7.5% -> 11-18%, with false_fix_rate 17% -> 12-17% (members whose features are survey-invariant agree on 2024 frames for the same reason they agree on training frames, so the confident set is enriched for correct fixes). 2024 coverage: 0.245 -> 0.28-0.40; the 0.2 FAIL floor is the explicit risk of adding a constraint to already-underfit members and is flagged, not hidden. 2024 median error among confident frames (1,342 m) should fall below 700 m. train_capture_diagnostics (bb_dop20 / truedop_2022 / truedop_2023 = 0.833 / 0.845 / 0.703 on exp 7, usable 22 / 18 / 32%) are predicted to stay within 0.65-0.90 and may drift slightly worse: the easiest fit is forbidden, so train top1 under augmentation will read a little below exp 7's 0.35 per member; the evidence is the 2024-vs-training gap narrowing, not the training numbers. Decision rules: (a) inv < 0.10 AND 2024 usable up by >= 3 points with false fix not rising -> supported; feature invariance across three surveys reaches a fourth, and the next experiment restores fit on top of it (experiment 5's whole-frame trunk per member, which lifted training-survey usable to 72-81% but had nothing invariant to carry) or adds +-12 px vantage jitter. (b) inv < 0.10 but 2024 usable flat (<= 9.5%) -> invariance across THESE three surveys, genuinely achieved this time, does not transfer to a fourth; close the cross-survey consistency family for this era (this is the fair test experiments 3 and 6 were not) and move to vantage jitter, the mapping/query confidence split, or capacity. (c) inv stays >= 0.20 at INV_WEIGHT 10 -> the cross-entropy out-muscled the term again; rerun once with INV_WEIGHT 30 before concluding anything. (d) 2024 coverage < 0.2 (FAIL) -> the constraint made the members disagree more on the foreign photograph, not less; note it, and the next step is the same loss with the committee gate relaxed to the geometric mean, nothing else changed. Standing check: the score must move through usable_fix_rate; an improvement through false_fix_rate alone with usable flat means the term taught honesty, not place - still kept, but rule (b) applies to the next design.
eli5: Each of the drone's two navigators boils a photo down to a short description of the place it is looking at - 112 numbers. We checked what happens to that description when the SAME spot is shown in two of the training photographs taken in different years: it changes by about a third of the amount it would change if you showed a completely different place, and most of that change is season and shadow, not geography. So the navigators have partly been describing the photograph rather than the ground, and a brand-new photograph gets a description that matches nowhere. The fix is a rule during training: every time a spot is shown in all three photographs at once, the three descriptions must come out the same, judged against how much descriptions differ between places. Whatever in a description tracks the time of year gets squeezed out; whatever tracks the streets and buildings stays. Nothing the drone carries changes - only what it was taught to pay attention to.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: two independent small strided conv stacks (112 channels at the top), sharing no weights; each turns the frame into its own compact 112-number description of the place. Unchanged at inference; during training this description is the tensor the new invariance rule reads

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor feeds its own scorer over all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin; the two tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: every mini-batch holds each place in all three training photographs at the same heading, each re-photographed at random; besides its own tile-and-offset loss, each member pays for any part of its 112-number place description that differs between the three photographs of the same place, measured against how much descriptions differ between places (within-place variance of the batch-standardised feature, weight 10). Paired three-survey batches, re-photographing, targets, schedule and views per epoch unchanged.

=== model/model.py ===
1. Add module constant INV_WEIGHT = 10.0 (weight of the cross-survey invariance loss). Keep CELL_PX, N_MEMBERS, MEMBER_CHANS, grid_dims(), build_model(), loss_fn() (signature AND body unchanged), export_onnx() and estimate_position() exactly as they are. Update the module docstring with one paragraph on the invariance term (keep the contract paragraph: 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1] -> [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalised map coords, conf in [0,1]; whole decode inside the graph).
2. Member.forward(self, x) returns THREE tensors: f = self.features(x).mean(dim=(2, 3)); return self.cls_head(f), torch.tanh(self.off_head(f)) * 0.5, f. f is the post-ReLU global-average-pooled [B, 112] feature - exactly the tensor the two heads read; nothing else about Member changes.
3. CellLocNet.training_outputs(self, x) returns the list of N_MEMBERS (logits, offset, feat) triples. CellLocNet.forward (the DEPLOYED decode) unpacks accordingly: ps = [F.softmax(l, dim=1) for l, _, _ in outs]; off = torch.stack([o for _, o, _ in outs], 0).mean(0); every other line stays byte-identical (pbar, argmax, block_mask, min-of-members conf, pooled centroid, clamp). The feature is already an intermediate node of the exported graph (/members.k/ReduceMean_output_0), so the ONNX must still be exactly 3,942,411 bytes - check this after export in your smoke test.
4. New function, next to loss_fn:

def invariance_loss(feat: torch.Tensor, n_caps: int, eps: float = 1e-5) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Cross-survey within-place variance fraction. feat is [P*K, D] with rows POSITION-MAJOR (row p*K + k = position p, capture k). Standardise every dimension over the whole batch, group into [P, K, D], and return the mean squared deviation from each position's own mean, scaled by K/(K-1) so unrelated views read 1.0 and identical views read 0.0. No detach anywhere: the batch std in the denominator carries gradient on purpose (VICReg's variance term in disguise); the cross-entropy on the same vector prevents collapse. K < 2 -> 0."""
    if n_caps < 2:
        return feat.new_zeros(())
    z = (feat - feat.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)) / (feat.std(dim=0, keepdim=True) + eps)
    z = z.view(-1, n_caps, feat.shape[1])
    within = ((z - z.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)) ** 2).mean()
    return within * (n_caps / (n_caps - 1))

=== model/train.py ===
5. Import INV_WEIGHT and invariance_loss from model.model.
6. POSITION-GROUPED MINI-BATCHES in run_epoch(). chunk_views() already returns its rows position-major (repeat_interleave(n_caps): row p*n_caps + k is position p in capture k) - rely on that and assert n == (n // n_caps) * n_caps once per chunk. Replace `perm = torch.randperm(n).to(device)` and the `for i in range(0, n, BATCH_SIZE): idx = perm[i:i + BATCH_SIZE]` loop with: n_pos = n // n_caps; pos_per_batch = max(1, BATCH_SIZE // n_caps) (= 21 positions = 63 views for three captures; compute it once in train_area or at the top of run_epoch); pos_perm = torch.randperm(n_pos, device=device); cap_off = torch.arange(n_caps, device=device); for i in range(0, n_pos, pos_per_batch): pidx = pos_perm[i:i + pos_per_batch]; idx = (pidx.unsqueeze(1) * n_caps + cap_off).reshape(-1). The last batch of a chunk may hold fewer positions; that is fine. Everything downstream of idx is unchanged: cap_b = cap_idx[idx], xb0 = gpu_crops(scene, cap_b, cx[idx], cy[idx], ang[idx]), cb/pb, soft_t = make_soft_targets(...), and each member STILL gets its own independent augment_views(xb0) draw.
7. Per member inside the batch: logits_k, off_k, feat_k = member(xb_k); off_t_k = residual_offset_target(model, logits_k, pb, meta) (unchanged); inv_k = invariance_loss(feat_k, n_caps); loss = loss + loss_fn(logits_k, off_k, soft_t, off_t_k) + INV_WEIGHT * inv_k. Accumulate inv_sum[k] += inv_k.detach() * B into a device-resident tensor of shape [N_MEMBERS] (same discipline as the existing counters: no .item()/.cpu()/float() inside the step loop).
8. Cross-survey argmax agreement, per member, on device: a = member_logits[k].argmax(dim=1).view(-1, n_caps); xagree[k] += (a == a[:, :1]).all(dim=1).long().sum(); xagree_seen += a.shape[0] (positions, counted once per batch). Keep the existing member_correct / agree (between members) / cap_correct / conf_sum statistics exactly as they are.
9. run_epoch returns additionally 'inv_sum' (list of N_MEMBERS floats), 'xagree' (list of N_MEMBERS ints) and 'xagree_seen' (int). train_area prints per epoch, appended to the existing line: inv=[per-member mean inv_sum/seen, 4 dp] xsurvey_agree=[per-member xagree/xagree_seen, 4 dp]. Update the module docstring (one paragraph on the invariance term and the position-grouped batches; note that experiment 3's raw-cosine version was vacuous because post-ReLU GAP features of different places already have cosine 0.70, which is why this one standardises per dimension first).
10.
